passage.quote:
An accuracy guarantee covers every permitted result for all inputs satisfying
its stated conditions.

summary: Represent a finite binary32 error neighborhood without selecting one permitted output or treating exceptional encodings as real numbers.
Combine the distance from a rounded center with the center’s error relative to the ideal real result; keep source interpretation and instruction execution separate.
Construct finite encoded rounded centers from input range bounds, and provide encoded nearest-even reciprocal arithmetic with explicit range/error guarantees.
Distinguish center-spacing, output-spacing and neighboring-encoding interpretations of ULP; do not silently treat one as PTX semantics.
Cover center-based and output-based ULP allowances in one finite relation and bound every permitted result without assuming its output range.
Derive natural-exponential error and encoded arithmetic witnesses from a concrete base-conversion constant, actual multiplication, and explicit input bounds; retain inherited shift error separately.
remaining: Conservative center/output ULP bounds and actual encoded base-conversion error/existence are proved, alongside finite centers and the accepted rounded reciprocal provider. Shift/subtraction, source interpretation and exceptional/overflow cases for a fetched exponential, and parallel kernel execution remain unfinished.

from.quote:
An approximate instruction may return several different bit patterns for the
same inputs. Its accuracy contract must cover every permitted result. A finite
error neighborhood contains binary32 words whose real values lie within a stated
absolute distance of a finite center word. An exceptional value, such as infinity
or NaN (not a number), does not belong to this finite neighborhood. Exceptional
instruction behavior therefore needs a separate contract.

passage.quote:
def Within (radius : ℝ) (center output : Word) : Prop :=
  ∃ c z : ℝ, finiteReal center = some c ∧ finiteReal output = some z ∧ |z-c| ≤ radius

from.quote:
The distance can be expressed in units in the last place, abbreviated ULP. This
is the spacing of the binary32 grid at a chosen real value, with a smallest step
of 2^-149 near zero. The chosen convention uses the pinned FloatLib/TorchLean ULP
at the center. At a power-of-two boundary, the spacing changes, so this convention
is explicit. A numerical neighborhood is not a claim that NVIDIA uses exactly
this convention, nor that every included bit pattern is physically realizable.

passage.quote:
def WithinULP (count : ℕ) (center output : Word) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, finiteReal center = some c ∧ Within (count * ulp32 c) center output

from.quote:
A nonnegative-radius neighborhood always contains its finite center. Membership
provides an actual finite real value and an absolute distance bound. If the
center is itself within error E of the ideal result, all members are within the
neighborhood radius plus E. In particular, a correctly rounded real center
contributes its rounding error in addition to the approximation allowance.
Theorems must not discard that extra rounding term.

passage.quote:
theorem rounded_center_error (h : Within radius center output)
    (value : finiteReal center = some (round32 ideal)) :
    ∃ z : ℝ, finiteReal output = some z ∧ |z-ideal| ≤ radius+eps32 ideal :=
  total_error h value (TorchLean.Floats.FP32.round_abs_error ideal)

from.quote:
A zero-radius neighborhood means equal real values, not necessarily equal bits:
the two signed zeros have the same real value. Instruction rules must add their
required sign and exceptional-value conditions. Widening an allowed radius can
only add outcomes. Several distinct finite words can satisfy a positive-radius
contract; no deterministic reference is silently substituted for those choices.

passage.quote:
theorem multiple_results : (0x3f800000 : Word) ≠ 0x3f800001 ∧
    Within ((2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ)) 0x3f800000 0x3f800000 ∧
    Within ((2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ)) 0x3f800000 0x3f800001 := by
  refine ⟨by decide, center_mem _ (by decide) _ (by positivity),
    1, 1+(2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ), one_real, successor_one_real, ?_⟩
  norm_num

from.quote:
A finite center can be constructed from any real input whose absolute value is
at most binary32's largest finite value. Round that input to the nearest grid
point, resolving exact halfway cases toward the value with an even final binary
digit, and encode the resulting integer times a power of two. Monotonicity of
rounding proves that this grid point is still within the finite range. The
encoding theorem returns an actual word and proves that its finite real value
is the rounded input; it does not assume output finiteness or representability.
This is a mathematical, non-executable construction for relational semantics,
not a software implementation of an exponential.

passage.quote:
theorem exists_word (x : ℝ) (range : |x| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite) :
    ∃ w : Word, finiteReal w = some (round32 x) :=
  ⟨word x, word_real x range⟩

theorem word_real (x : ℝ) (range : |x| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite) :
    finiteReal (word x) = some (round32 x) := by
  rw [finiteReal_some _ (word_finite x range)]
  have h := Model.isFinite_roundDyadic_of_isIEEE_of_abs_toReal_le_posMaxFinite
    FloatFormat.binary32 (by decide) (roundedDyadic x)
    (by rw [roundedDyadic_real]; exact round_range x range)
  rw [word, decode_bits]
  apply congrArg some
  exact (Model.toReal_roundDyadic_eq_roundAt _ (by decide) _ h).trans
    (by rw [roundedDyadic_real]; exact round_idempotent x)

from.quote:
For nonpositive arguments, a base-two exponential lies between zero and one;
for arguments at least one, a reciprocal lies between zero and one. These input
domains therefore admit finite rounded centers, including gradual underflow to
zero. They are useful sufficient domains for stable softmax, not the full PTX
instruction domains. The approximate-result relation still permits every word
in its stated neighborhood rather than replacing that relation by its center.
For an ideal value between zero and one, both it and its rounded center have
ULP at most 2^-23. A count-k neighborhood therefore has total absolute error at
most (k+1/2)*2^-23. For the two-ULP exponential allowance this is 5*2^-24.
This conservative estimate includes rounding and does not assert that an
instruction attains every included value.

passage.quote:
theorem exp2_results_exists (count : ℕ) (x : ℝ) (nonpos : x ≤ 0) :
    ∃ output, Results count ((2:ℝ)^x) output :=
  results_exists count _ (exp2_range x nonpos)

theorem results_error (count : ℕ) (x : ℝ) (output : Word)
    (nonneg : 0 ≤ x) (upper : x ≤ 1) (allowed : RoundedReal.Results count x output) :
    ∃ z : ℝ, finiteReal output = some z ∧
      |z-x| ≤ ((count:ℝ)+1/2)*(2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ) := by
  obtain ⟨z,hz,bound⟩ := RoundedReal.results_error count x output
    (RoundedReal.unit_range x nonneg upper) allowed
  refine ⟨z,hz,bound.trans ?_⟩
  have rounded := round_unit x nonneg upper
  have allowance := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
    (ulp_unit (round32 x) rounded.1 rounded.2) (Nat.cast_nonneg count : (0:ℝ) ≤ count)
  have rounding : eps32 x ≤ (2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ)/2 :=
    div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (ulp_unit x nonneg upper) (by norm_num)
  calc
    _ ≤ count * (2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ) + (2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ)/2 := add_le_add allowance rounding
    _ = _ := by ring

from.quote:
The reciprocal provider uses nearest-even division of the encoded value one by
the actual encoded operand. The fetched rcp.rn.f32 instruction preserves exactly
this result relation and checks the selected PTX version and target. A nonzero
finite operand and a bound on the exact quotient establish finite output and
the rounded-real meaning of every permitted result. These are numerical-analysis
conditions, not restrictions on instruction execution. The NaN envelope preserves
the existing uncertainty about permitted NaN payloads. Approximate reciprocal
and its error convention remain separate work.

passage.quote:
theorem results_real (input output : Word) (x : ℝ) (value : finiteReal input = some x)
    (nonzero : x ≠ 0) (range : |1/x| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite) (allowed : Results input output) :
    finiteReal output = some (round32 (1/x)) := by
  rw [envelope_finite_eq _ _ (reference_finite input x value nonzero range) allowed]
  exact reference_real input x value nonzero range

from.quote:
Measuring ULP at the output can permit a value excluded by measuring it at the
center. A checked boundary example uses center 1/2-2^-25 and output 1/2+2^-24:
their distance is three center steps but only one and a half output steps.
Thus the center convention cannot be called a conservative replacement for the
output convention. This example distinguishes numerical policies; it does not
claim that a GPU produces that output or that this center is reached by an
encoded exponential operand. A source-faithful exponential contract still needs
an explicit interpretation policy and separate exceptional-value cases.

passage.quote:
theorem output_spacing_not_center_spacing :
    |output-center| ≤ 2*ulp32 output ∧
      ¬ Approximate.WithinULP 2 0x3effffff 0x3f000001 := by
  constructor
  · rw [output_ulp]; norm_num [center, output]
  · rintro ⟨c, hc, c', z, hc', hz, bound⟩
    rw [center_real] at hc hc'
    rw [output_real] at hz
    cases Option.some.inj hc
    cases Option.some.inj hc'
    cases Option.some.inj hz
    rw [center_ulp] at bound
    norm_num [center, output] at bound

A second neighborhood deliberately covers both choices of where to measure ULP:
at the finite center and at the finite returned value. It uses the larger of
these two spacings. Every result admitted by either choice belongs to this
neighborhood, and the center itself is an encoded witness that it is nonempty.
This covers these two named interpretations only; it does not establish that
NVIDIA uniquely specifies either one or cover an unproved interpretation based
on counting adjacent encodings.

theorem within_iff (count : ℕ) (center output : Word) :

      Approximate.WithinULP count center output ∨ OutputULP count center output := by

  · rintro ⟨c,z,hc,hz,bound⟩
    rcases le_total (ulp32 c) (ulp32 z) with h | h
    · right; exact ⟨c,z,hc,hz,by simpa [max_eq_right h] using bound⟩
    · left; exact ⟨c,hc,c,z,hc,hz,by simpa [max_eq_left h] using bound⟩
  · intro h; exact h.elim center_included output_included

from.quote:
For a center between zero and one, a two-ULP result in this wider neighborhood
still has distance at most 2*2^-23 from the center. This bound is derived without
assuming that the returned value lies between zero and one: a global bound on
spacing first constrains its magnitude, and then the local spacing bound applies.
Adding nearest-even rounding error gives absolute error at most 5*2^-24 from an
ideal value between zero and one. Hence the same numerical error budget can be
used for a nonpositive base-two exponential under either named interpretation.
The relation retains signed zeros and possible tiny negative results; special
instruction cases and any source-mandated sign conditions remain separate.

passage.quote:
theorem unit_distance (c z : ℝ) (nonneg : 0 ≤ c) (upper : c ≤ 1)
    (allowed : |z-c| ≤ 2 * max (ulp32 c) (ulp32 z)) :
    |z-c| ≤ 2 * (2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ) := by
  have center := ApproximateBounds.ulp_unit c nonneg upper
  have coarse := ulp_coarse z
  have triangle : |z| ≤ |z-c| + 1 := by
    have := abs_sub_le z c 0
    simp only [sub_zero, abs_of_nonneg nonneg] at this
    exact this.trans (add_le_add_right upper _)
  have loose : max (ulp32 c) (ulp32 z) ≤ (|z|+1)*(2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ) := by
    apply max_le _ coarse
    apply center.trans
    norm_num
  have distance := allowed.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left loose (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 2))
  have small : |z| < 2 := by
    norm_num at distance
    linarith
  exact allowed.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
    (max_le center (ulp_below_two z small)) (by norm_num))

passage.quote:
theorem results_error (x : ℝ) (output : Word) (nonneg : 0 ≤ x) (upper : x ≤ 1)
    (allowed : Results x output) :
    ∃ z : ℝ, finiteReal output = some z ∧ |z-x| ≤ 5/(2:ℝ)^24 := by
  obtain ⟨c,z,hc,hz,bound⟩ := allowed
  have same : c = round32 x := Option.some.inj
    (hc.symm.trans (RoundedReal.word_real x (RoundedReal.unit_range x nonneg upper)))
  subst c
  have rounded := ApproximateBounds.round_unit x nonneg upper
  have distance := unit_distance _ _ rounded.1 rounded.2 (by simpa using bound)
  have rounding := TorchLean.Floats.FP32.round_abs_error x
  have eps : eps32 x ≤ (2:ℝ)^(-23:ℤ)/2 :=
    div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (ApproximateBounds.ulp_unit x nonneg upper) (by norm_num)
  refine ⟨z,hz,?_⟩
  have := (abs_sub_le z (round32 x) x).trans (add_le_add distance (rounding.trans eps))
  norm_num at this ⊢
  exact this

from.quote:
Converting a natural exponential to base two uses a concrete binary32 constant,
0x3fb8aa3b, approximating 1/log(2), and an ordinary rounded multiplication by
that constant. Its error budget keeps three contributions visible: any error
already present in the shifted input, the constant's error, and multiplication
rounding. For nonpositive inputs, rounding preserves the nonpositive sign;
the exponential sensitivity bound then carries argument error to output error.
A finite multiplication result requires a bound on the exact product before
rounding. The resulting theorem applies to actual encoded multiplication and
approximate outputs, but does not claim that a fetched kernel has performed the
shift, multiplication, or exponential. It leaves the constant's error as an
explicit real expression, not an unverified decimal estimate.

passage.quote:
theorem constant_real : finiteReal constantWord = some constantValue := by
  rw [finiteReal_some _ (by decide)]
  change some (Model.toReal (Model.ofFields FloatFormat.binary32 false 127 3713595)) = _
  rw [Model.toReal_ofFields_normal _ _ _ _ (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)]
  norm_num [constantValue, FloatFormat.binary32, Model.pow2, bpow, binaryRadix, Radix.toReal]

passage.quote:
theorem natural_exp_error (x t shiftError : ℝ) (input product output : Word)
    (value : finiteReal input = some x) (nonpos : x ≤ 0) (idealNonpos : t ≤ 0)
    (range : |x*constantValue| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite) (shift : |x-t| ≤ shiftError)
    (multiply : Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul input constantWord product)
    (approximate : FiniteExp2 product output) :
    ∃ z : ℝ, finiteReal output = some z ∧
      |z-Real.exp t| ≤ 5/(2:ℝ)^24 + Real.log 2 * budget x shiftError := by
  have pr := product_real input product x value nonpos range multiply
  obtain ⟨a,ha,err⟩ := argument_error x t shiftError input product value range shift multiply
  have same : a = round32 (x*constantValue) := Option.some.inj (ha.symm.trans pr.1)
  subst a
  obtain ⟨a,ha,_,approximate⟩ := approximate
  have same : a = round32 (x*constantValue) := Option.some.inj (ha.symm.trans pr.1)
  subst a
  obtain ⟨z,hz,approx⟩ := ConservativeULP.exp2_error _ output pr.2 approximate
  have logpos : 0 < Real.log 2 := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)
  have sensitivity := exp2_nonpos_distance (round32 (x*constantValue)) (t/Real.log 2)
    pr.2 (div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg idealNonpos logpos.le)
  rw [base_conversion] at sensitivity
  exact ⟨z,hz,(abs_sub_le _ _ _).trans (add_le_add approx
    (sensitivity.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left err logpos.le)))⟩

theorem stages_exist (input : Word) (x : ℝ) (value : finiteReal input = some x)
    (nonpos : x ≤ 0) (range : |x*constantValue| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite) :
    ∃ product output, Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul input constantWord product ∧
      finiteReal product = some (round32 (x*constantValue)) ∧
      FiniteExp2 product output := by
  obtain ⟨product,allowed⟩ := Ptx.Binary32.results_exists .mul input constantWord
  have pr := product_real input product x value nonpos range allowed
  obtain ⟨output,h⟩ := ConservativeULP.exp2_results_exists _ pr.2
  exact ⟨product,output,allowed,pr.1,_,pr.1,pr.2,h⟩

theorem bounded_product_range (x : ℝ) (small : |x| ≤ (2:ℝ)^(126:ℤ)) :
    |x*constantValue| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite := by
  rw [abs_mul,abs_of_pos constant_positive]
  have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right small constant_positive.le
  apply h.trans
  rw [Bounds.maxFinite_eq]
  norm_num [constantValue]
